does: Fries coated croquetas in a few at a time in hot oil deep enough to cover them, turning them until the shell is deep golden all round and the paste inside has melted soft.

intro.what: Frying croquetas turns their coating into a crisp golden shell around a soft paste.
intro.why: It teaches you to keep frying heat steady and turn a delicate shell without piercing it.

how: Heat plenty of oil in a deep, heavy pan. A crumb dropped in should sizzle at once and rise.
Lower a few croquetas in with a slotted spoon. Do not crowd the pan, or the oil cools and the shells go greasy.
Turn them gently until they are deep golden all round.
Lift them out onto a rack and let the oil run off. Serve at once, while the shell is crisp and the middle is soft.

cues.text: A sharp, steady sizzle when they go in, which quietens as the shell sets.
The shell is an even deep gold, with no cracks.
The croquetas are light for their size and the shell feels firm when pressed.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is not hot enough, so that the shell soaks up oil and the paste leaks out.
mistakes.fix: Wait until a crumb sizzles at once, and fry only a few at a time.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, which cools the oil.
mistakes.fix: Fry in small batches and let the oil heat up again between them.

mistakes.mistake: Piercing the shell with a fork while turning.
mistakes.fix: Turn them with a slotted spoon.

quiz.question: Why fry croquetas in small batches?
choices: To keep the coating pale and soft.
To avoid cooling the oil and making the shells greasy.
To let the shells press tightly against each other.
quiz.because: Crowding lowers the oil heat, which can make the shell absorb oil and leak.

quiz.question: How should you turn them?
choices: By piercing the shell with a fork.
By squeezing the middle firmly with a fork.
quiz.because: A slotted spoon turns the croqueta without puncturing its coating.

quiz.question: Which shell appearance is the aim?
choices: A pale shell with paste leaking through cracks.
Dark patches around a wet coating.
quiz.because: An evenly coloured intact shell is the intended result of gentle frying and turning.

quiz.question: The oil cools when a large batch goes in. What would you change for the next batch?
choices: Add the next batch before the oil recovers.
Fry fewer and let the oil heat up again.
Keep the pan tightly packed to stop movement.
quiz.because: Smaller batches and reheating address the drop in oil heat caused by crowding.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to fry until the croquetas are shaped and coated.

variant_of.differs: The food is a soft paste in a fragile shell that has to set in the first moments, so the oil must be hot at once and only a few go in each time. A firm food such as a potato is fried to cook it and then fried again to crisp it.
